rules.topic: IE energy wires (server config defaults; EnergyWireConfig args are max length, transfer rate IF/t, loss ratio per 16 blocks): copper wire max length 16, 2048 IF/t, 5 percent loss per 16 blocks; electrum wire length 16, 8192 IF/t, 2.5 percent per 16 blocks (line 59); HV steel wire length 32, 32768 IF/t, 2.5 percent per 16 blocks (line 63)

rules.quote: .comment("In- and output rates of "+name+" wire connectors. This is independant of the transferrate of the wires.")
rules.topic: Wire connectors are the real bottleneck: a connector's in/out rate defaults to the wire transfer rate divided by 8 (copper 256 IF/t, electrum 1024 IF/t, HV 4096 IF/t per connector), independent of the wire's own rate - feeding a hungry machine takes multiple connectors or a higher tier
Capacitor storage tiers (config defaults: capacity IF, input IF/t, output IF/t): LV 100000 IF at 256/256, MV 1000000 IF at 1024/1024 (line 149), HV 4000000 IF at 4096/4096 (line 150)
The diesel generator produces 4096 IF/t by default (config dieselGen_output, defined at line 164) when burning biodiesel or other accepted fuels; per-fuel burn times are recipe data

rules.quote: excavator_consumption = addPositive(builder, "consumption", 4096, "The Flux per tick the Excavator will consume to dig");
rules.topic: The bucket-wheel excavator consumes 4096 IF/t while digging a mineral deposit; deposits themselves (vein types, sizes, biome/dimension placement) are datapack data in the jar, so quote deposit facts from layer-2 extraction, not from code

Most IE machines (crusher, arc furnace, squeezer, fermenter, refinery, mixer, metal press...) take their energy cost and processing time from recipe data, with per-machine energy/time modifier config values (default 1.0) on top - per-recipe numbers come from the jar's recipe JSONs, not from constants
